summary: Review Petition against the Order dated 2.5.2025 passed in Petition No. 281/GT/2020 Under Section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 52 of the CERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 read with Section 114 and Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 3. The Review Petitioner has further submitted that, notwithstanding the fact that the Commission condoned the entire time overrun in the commissioning of both the Units, a part of its claim towards notional IDC was disallowed. The Review Petitioner has requested review of the said disallowance, including the disallowance of notional IDC pertaining to the period prior to the date of IA. 4. On 27.11.2025, the instant Review Petition was ‘admitted,’ and notices were issued to the Respondents to complete their pleadings in the matter. 9. The Review Petition was heard in detail, and, after hearing the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner, an order in the matter was reserved. 10. We have considered the submissions of the Review Petitioner, the reply filed by the Respondent UPPCL, and its rejoinder submitted by the Review Petitioner. Now, we proceed to consider whether any case for review has been made out by the Review Petitioner in terms of Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 (hereinafter “Conduct of Business Regulations”). - _(a) by a decree or order from which an appeal is allowed, but from which no appeal has been preferred,_ _and who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made, or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review of the decree passed or order made against him, may apply for a review of judgment to the Court which passed the decree or made the order._ _(2) A party who is not appealing from a decree or order may apply for a review of judgment notwithstanding the pendency of an appeal by some other party except where the ground of such appeal is common to the applicant and the appellant, or when, being respondent, he can present to the Appellate Court the case on which he applied for the review._ _Explanation.—The fact that the decision on a question of law on which the judgment of the Court is based has been reversed or modified by the subsequent decision of a superior Court in any other case, shall not be a ground for the review of such judgment.”_ A bare reading of these relevant legal provisions would make it clear that an application for review of an order is maintainable upon (i) discovery of a new and important matter or evidence which, after exercise of due diligence, was not within the knowledge of the review applicant or could not be produced by him when the judgment/order was passed; or (ii) on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of record; or (iii) for any other sufficient reason. substitute a view for the reason that a Review Petition cannot be permitted to be an appeal in disguise. 12. The Review Petitioner has sought review of paragraphs 62 and 68 of the impugned order on the following grounds: 13. The Review Petitioner has claimed notional IDC from the 4 th Quarter of 201314, whereas the IA for the Project was accorded only on 10.9.2014. The Review Petitioner has submitted that the initial deployment of funds, including the funds deployed prior to the IA, was made from shareholders' funds and that the absence of actual debt during such period cannot be a ground for denial of normative IDC. The Review Petitioner has relied upon Regulations 18, 19(2)(b) and 21 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations and the judgment of the APTEL dated 28.2.2025 in Appeal No. 212 of 2017 in support of its contention. > _“16. We have considered the above submissions of the Petitioner. However, under the extant regulatory framework, Regulation 21(2) of the 2019 Tariff_ 16. The Review Petitioner has also relied upon the judgment dated 28.2.2025 of the APTEL in Appeal No. 212 of 2017. The said judgment dealt with the denial of normative IDC on the ground that actual debt had not been drawn and the project was funded through internal resources. It did not deal with the admissibility of normative IDC for the period prior to the IA. Therefore, the said judgment does not support Review Petitioner’s claim for normative IDC for the period prior to the IA. 22. It is noted that the Review Petitioner has relied upon the Commission's order dated 17.4.2025 in Review Petition No. 11/RP/2024 in Petition No. 421/GT/2020 wherein the issue was the period up to which normative IDC was to be computed after condonation of delay. The same principle has already been applied in the Instant case also, as normative IDC has been computed up to the actual CODs and not restricted to the original SCOD. The said order, therefore, does not support allowability of the entire amount claimed by the Review Petitioner. 24. By way of the instant Review Petition, the Review Petitioner is actually seeking a relook of the order under review in the hope to discover any flaw or fault in the same, which is not permissible in law. Hence, we are of the considered opinion that the Review Petitioner has failed to make out any mistake or error apparent on the face of record in the order under review dated 2.5.2025.
